thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — Geographical DNS mismatch detected between Cloudflare and Route53 for service.example.redwood.com. Elevated 5xx rates observed in EU-West and APAC regions. Auto-escalating to network oncall.

alice (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm taking lead. TL;DR: some resolvers are returning older A records pointing at EU-primary while Route53 health checks are flapping; Cloudflare is serving inconsistent authoritative answers in different POPs. Impact: partial traffic diversion, client-side TLS handshakes failing for a subset of customers.

devon (network): I'm pulling up dig traces and health-check history. Initial dig from our vantage points:

```
# from 1.1.1.1 (cloudflare resolver)
dig +short service.example.redwood.com @1.1.1.1
3.4.5.6
\n# from 8.8.8.8 (google)
dig +short service.example.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
10.11.12.13
```

devon (network): Cloudflare authoritative returns the EU-primary IP in multiple PoPs, but Route53 geo record set sometimes returns the APAC IP. TTLs look odd: Cloudflare set TTL 300s, Route53 60s historically but due to a recent config rollback one zone had TTL 86400 for a subset of records. That causes long-lived caches to persist.

samir (sre): Observed 2.3% aggregate error increase for EU-west customer requests, spike start ~14:10 UTC. Alerting rules firing for 5xx and TLS failures. Route53 health checks showing intermittent failures for the origin group EU-primary since 14:05 UTC.

opsbot: Attached runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dns-failover (private).

lucy (product): I'm drafting a customer-facing status note. Short version: "We detected DNS routing inconsistencies causing partial connectivity issues for customers in Europe and APAC; teams are actively remediating."

alice (oncall): Immediate mitigations I'm pushing: 1) Force GeoDNS to use weighted failover with EU->fallback to global-secondary; 2) Temporarily set authoritative TTL to 60s on Cloudflare; 3) Pause any recent Route53 config rollouts. Devon, can you update Cloudflare TTL and confirm propagation?

devon (network): Doing Cloudflare TTL change now, setting to 60. Also opening Cloudflare dashboard to check recent deployments. Cloudflare status shows "increased propagation latency" for a subset of POPs: https://status.cloudflare.com/incidents/XYZ (internal link).

devon (network): Route53 note: there was a partial rollback last night that left an outdated geo record in the APAC bucket with TTL 86400. I'm marking that record for deletion. Running AWS check: `aws route53 list-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZONE123 --query 'ResourceRecordSets[?Name==\`service.example.redwood.com.\`]'`

samir (sre): Applying traffic mitigation via Redwood Console: updated GeoDNS policy to prefer global-secondary in EU until Route53 is cleaned. Applied at 14:37 UTC.

incident-bot: Change applied: GeoDNS policy updated by samir at 1769800620. Automated monitors will report in 5m.

devon (network): After changes, sample dig traces:
```
dig +short service.example.redwood.com @1.1.1.1
10.11.12.13
\ndig +short service.example.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
10.11.12.13
```
devon (network): Looks like Cloudflare authoritative answers are beginning to converge to the secondary IP. But reminder: many client-side resolvers still cache the old EU-primary IP due to earlier high TTLs. We will see gradual falloff over TTL window.

lucy (product): Customer impact update: we've identified ~12 enterprise customers that hit repeated TLS handshake errors. CS notified and provided mitigation (client flush DNS + retry). Draft status posted to status.redwood.com/incident/1769800000 (draft).

samir (sre): Error rate dropped from 2.3% -> 0.6% in 20 minutes after failover. Some resolvers (corporate proxies) still serving old records. Recommend adding short-lived HTTP-level redirects from old IP to new one as an extra safety net — engineering needs to confirm certificates/cors.

devon (network): Confirmed Route53 record with TTL 86400 has been removed at 14:42 UTC and new Geo set to 60s. AWS health check flapping persists for EU-primary; we should keep it out of rotation until stable.

alice (oncall): Action list for handoff: 1) Monitor error rate and TLS handshake errors for next 4h. 2) Keep TTL low (60s) until global propagation stabilizes. 3) Work with CS to contact the 12 impacted customers for cache flush guidance. 4) Keep Route53 geo off the EU-primary until health checks stable for 30m.

maria (oncall-2nd): I'm taking night handoff at 18:00 UTC. Leaving note: watch for residual cache issues from APAC corporate resolvers; call devon if terrain reappears. I have access to Cloudflare and AWS consoles.

alice (oncall): Handoff checklist posted to thread. Leaving at 18:00 UTC.

cloudflare-bot: Noted propagation delays in several PoPs; expected full convergence within TTL window (60s) + client cache variance.

samir (sre): Final check at 15:20 UTC: error rates back within normal band, customer retries succeeding. I'll keep monitors at elevated sensitivity for 2 hours before closing.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 1769800800. Monitoring-only state.

maria (oncall-2nd): ACK. I'll update the runbook with exact commands run and record the Route53 record id removed. Also will follow up on permanent fix to avoid config rollback reintroducing long TTLs.

alice (oncall): Summary for postmortem: root cause: misaligned TTL and an inadvertent Route53 rollback that reintroduced an old geo record; Cloudflare propagation delays amplified the issue. Mitigations: forced failover via GeoDNS, lowered TTLs, removed stale Route53 entries. Next steps: add a safety check to pre-merge tests to prevent TTL=86400 for geo records and add a post-deploy verification that authoritative answers match expected IP sets.

lucy (product): I'll prepare customer communication and a follow-up note once postmortem is ready.

incident-bot: Thread will remain open for handoff notes and postmortem link.
